edits.title: Resolve semantic findings and verify recovery claims against actual results
edits.content:
A passing schema, quote-membership check, or constraint log does not establish semantic completeness. When an audit identifies additional historical affiliations or other omitted values, resolve the finding against the requested field definition and dated evidence. Do not dismiss concurrent or honorary affiliations solely because a preferred announcement omits them: 'affiliation at award' and 'affiliation listed by the awarding body' are different scopes. Verify whether the additional positions applied at the relevant date, then include supported values or document an evidence-based exclusion. An inconclusive follow-up search does not resolve the finding. Only mark the semantic constraint satisfied after this reconciliation.

Recovery summaries and refinement requests must reflect observed results. Successful downloads and schema-valid extraction can still yield no supported values for the missing field. Before claiming recovery, inspect the returned cells and count newly supported values against the previous coverage. If the extraction returns empty cells, retain the gap and seek other evidence; do not describe an alternate format as supplying the missing information. Keep planned actions, successful retrieval, field recovery, and final submission distinct.

Targeted follow-up sources support checking concurrent affiliations and excluding appointments outside the requested period.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, no citations, and no constraint coverage. However, the visible trajectory ends during extraction, without a final submission or a recorded termination cause. This establishes an unfinished snapshot, not a supported diagnosis of forgotten submission, exhausted capacity, or a defective harness entry. No speculative completion rule is added.

All 20 occurrences concern verification of already discovered people: nine nationality searches, nine affiliation/date searches, and two alternate-format searches. Each returned hits and honestly recorded no new entities. The initial searches recorded 28 people successfully. Existing memory explicitly distinguishes verification from discovery, so these signals do not justify inventing discoveries or revising that guidance.

The seven failures comprise two AP HTTP 403 responses, a KVA redirect loop, an Austrian Academy HTTP 403 response, an INFN redirect loop, and two unreadable KIAS PDFs. Successful INFN and Nobel facts alternatives supplied affiliation evidence; alternate recent prize PDFs were located but their retrieval is not shown. KIAS and nationality recovery remain unresolved. Existing skill already covers alternate official sources, retaining successful downloads, and field-level validation. These failures do not establish consistently harmful guidance or support domain-wide exclusions.

The root code embeds a refinement focus claiming that PDFs supplied citizenship, but the seven subsequent extraction responses all preserve empty nationality values, sources, and quotes. The code would therefore accumulate zero nationality updates. The snapshot does not show the refinement call executing, so the supported failure is the premature success claim in its prepared focus. Extend the existing memory's distinction between mechanical validity and semantic completeness to recovery reporting.

The audit produced specific verification leads, and fetched institutional sources supplied concurrent appointments and dates for excluding later or ended positions. This supports the existing semantic-audit memory rather than demonstrating bad outcomes from it. Final reconciliation into rows is not visible, so neither a completed recovery claim nor a duplicate skill is warranted.

edits.title: Resolve semantic findings and validate quotation provenance before claiming recovery
edits.content:
A passing schema, quote-membership check, or constraint log does not establish semantic completeness. When an audit identifies additional historical affiliations or other omitted values, resolve the finding against the requested field definition and dated evidence. Do not dismiss concurrent or honorary affiliations solely because a preferred announcement omits them: 'affiliation at award' and 'affiliation listed by the awarding body' are different scopes. Verify whether the additional positions applied at the relevant date, then include supported values or document an evidence-based exclusion. An inconclusive follow-up search does not resolve the finding. Only mark the semantic constraint satisfied after this reconciliation.

Recovery summaries and refinement requests must reflect observed results. Successful downloads and schema-valid extraction can still yield no supported values for the missing field. Before claiming recovery, inspect the returned cells and count newly supported values against the previous coverage. If the extraction returns empty cells, retain the gap and seek other evidence; do not describe an alternate format as supplying the missing information. Keep planned actions, successful retrieval, field recovery, and final submission distinct.

Quotation validity is source-specific. A quote occurring in any one cited document does not validate that quote against every URL attached to the cell. Keep a claim-to-source-to-exact-span ledger and validate every emitted quote/source association, including auxiliary audit evidence and the final serialized output. In this run, any-source checks passed while six source associations across five cells failed the final check. These were provenance mismatches, not proof that the underlying claims or quotation text were invented.

Never splice excerpts from different sources, add quotation marks, normalize PDF spacing, or expand abbreviations inside a verbatim quote. Diagnose rejected patches with the failing source and exact span; repair from the retained source text and validate before applying. Recheck semantic support after repair because replacing a quote can change which claim it supports.

Respect the output representation: where separate quote/source pairs are supported, preserve each pair separately. Where one quote is applied to all listed sources, every listed source must contain that quote. Seek evidence that supports the complete value within that representation; do not merely drop necessary sources or retain unsupported value components to pass a check. If complete support cannot be represented, preserve the limitation through the permitted output mechanism. A model's supported flag or a constraint receipt for one matching source does not substitute for these checks.

edits.title: Recover primary-source evidence with bounded, source-preserving extraction
edits.content:
When a primary-source page fails to download, inspect the recorded failure and search for another official publication of the same material, including a downloadable PDF. Select an actual URL from search results, fetch it, and retain its text and URL together. Reuse successful downloads from the original batch. Group extraction by document when it covers several related entities, using an explicit nested schema. Check field coverage separately: a document may support names, dates, affiliations and award motivations without explicitly stating nationality or citizenship. Do not infer citizenship from birthplace or institutional location. Validate extracted quotations against the exact downloaded text before accepting records; PDF column layout and whitespace can affect verbatim quotations.

Before model extraction or review, bound the serialized request, not merely the number of documents or entities. A focused fetch can still return entire annual reports, archives, or garbled PDF text. Retain full downloaded snapshots locally, exclude failed-fetch sentinels, deduplicate documents, and select exact text windows around relevant entities and claims. Merge overlapping windows and retain URL, dates, headings, and enough context to interpret roles and timelines. Do not join windows into a purported contiguous quotation.

Measure the serialized prompt, allowing headroom for schema and transport overhead; split coherent evidence packets when necessary. A recovered input-limit failure in this run was resolved by replacing full reports with about 25,000 characters of relevant source windows. Inspect readability and widen or supplement windows when date or subject context is missing; absence from a selected window is not absence from the document.

After a failed call, inspect which earlier operations completed and preserve accepted updates and successful downloads. Retry only the failed review with bounded evidence, then validate returned source spans and field coverage. Successful retrieval alone does not establish recovery of the requested field.

decisions.reason: All six occurrences were inspected. Rows 4, 14, 19 and 20 each have one nonverbatim source association; row 24 has two. Every affected cell also has one matching source. The final code selects a matching source with next(), and earlier checks use any(), whereas the citation results evaluate each attached URL. Thus the concrete failure is per-source provenance, not demonstrated invention of all six quote strings. Existing generic quotation guidance did not prevent it; the memory update adds representation-aware validation without sacrificing semantic support.

All 52 occurrences concern verification after the initial ten discovery records identified 28 entities: nine group nationality searches, nine affiliation searches, two PDF searches, 26 individual nationality searches and six targeted follow-ups. All searches returned hits. Empty discovery arrays therefore do not establish stalled verification. The existing discovery memory explicitly requires honest empty records for known-entity verification, and the trajectory follows it. Its prior and current outcomes do not justify weakening or duplicating that guidance.

All 19 failures were reviewed: nine HTTP 403s, two HTTP 404s, three redirect loops, three unreadable-text failures, one timeout and one closed connection. Other sources and cached successes enabled progress; all final cited URLs have successful fetch records. The existing alternate-source skill already covers retaining successes and seeking actual alternative URLs. These observations do not establish successful repair of the failed endpoints or warrant endpoint-specific rules. The separate input-size candidate supports the targeted skill extension.

The call exceeded the 1,048,576-character input limit with 1,202,710 characters after five affiliation updates had already been accepted. Recovery retained those updates and used merged exact-source windows totaling 25,212 excerpt characters; the subsequent review completed without stderr. This successful repeatable recovery belongs in the existing evidence-extraction skill, with serialized-size checks before submission.

The assertion blocked a patch whose quote combined two source excerpts with added curly quotation marks. Diagnostics showed no unknown sources but no matching quotation. A single exact annual-report span repaired the patch, and later validation passed. Recovery is evidence for retaining the guard, not dismissing the failure; the provenance memory adds exact-span construction and targeted repair while addressing the remaining multi-source mismatch.

The execution reported zero nationality cells filled while submitting a recovery claim; the next diagnostic explicitly corrected that premise. Existing entry 2 already addresses this exact failure with measured before/after coverage and separate retrieval versus field recovery. Its version history includes the correction; the single recorded failed run does not show repeated failure of that revised instruction. No further edit is needed.

The auxiliary audit reported no unresolved support while deterministic membership testing found one PDF quotation mismatch. Inspection and exact-source replacement repaired it before finalization. This independently supports validating audit quotes rather than trusting semantic approval, and checking that the replacement still supports the stated claim. It shares the provenance update rather than creating a duplicate entry.

The reviewed records show useful reconciliation of dated roles, concurrent affiliations and later citizenship, plus full-source review of components omitted from selected quotations. They also show that reviewer objections need adjudication rather than automatic acceptance. Existing entry 2 already preserves this procedure and distinguishes semantic completeness from mechanical checks. Remaining quotation-provenance weaknesses are handled by the accepted update; no separate historical or benchmark-specific lesson is warranted.

If the extraction returns empty cells, retain the gap and seek other evidence; do not describe an alternate format as supplying the missing information. Keep planned actions, successful retrieval, field recovery, and final submission distinct.

Quotation validity is source-specific. A quote occurring in any one cited document does not validate that quote against every URL attached to the cell. Keep a claim-to-source-to-exact-span ledger and validate every emitted quote/source association, including auxiliary audit evidence and the final serialized output. In this run, any-source checks passed while six source associations across five cells failed the final check. These were provenance mismatches, not proof that the underlying claims or quotation text were invented.

Never splice excerpts from different sources, add quotation marks, normalize PDF spacing, or expand abbreviations inside a verbatim quote. Diagnose rejected patches with the failing source and exact span; repair from the retained source text and validate before applying. Recheck semantic support after repair because replacing a quote can change which claim it supports.

Respect the output representation: where separate quote/source pairs are supported, preserve each pair separately. Where one quote is applied to all listed sources, every listed source must contain that quote. Seek evidence that supports the complete value within that representation; do not merely drop necessary sources or retain unsupported value components to pass a check. If complete support cannot be represented, preserve the limitation through the permitted output mechanism. A model's supported flag or a constraint receipt for one matching source does not substitute for these checks.

edits.title: Recover primary-source evidence with bounded, source-preserving extraction
edits.content:
When a primary-source page fails to download, inspect the recorded failure and search for another official publication of the same material, including a downloadable PDF. Select an actual URL from search results, fetch it, and retain its text and URL together. Reuse successful downloads from the original batch. Group extraction by document when it covers several related entities, using an explicit nested schema. Check field coverage separately: a document may support names, dates, affiliations and award motivations without explicitly stating nationality or citizenship. Do not infer citizenship from birthplace or institutional location. Validate extracted quotations against the exact downloaded text before accepting records; PDF column layout and whitespace can affect verbatim quotations.

Before model extraction or review, bound the serialized request, not merely the number of documents or entities. A focused fetch can still return entire annual reports, archives, or garbled PDF text. Retain full downloaded snapshots locally, exclude failed-fetch sentinels, deduplicate documents, and select exact text windows around relevant entities and claims. Merge overlapping windows and retain URL, dates, headings, and enough context to interpret roles and timelines. Do not join windows into a purported contiguous quotation.

Measure the serialized prompt, allowing headroom for schema and transport overhead; split coherent evidence packets when necessary. A recovered input-limit failure in this run was resolved by replacing full reports with about 25,000 characters of relevant source windows. Inspect readability and widen or supplement windows when date or subject context is missing; absence from a selected window is not absence from the document.

After a failed call, inspect which earlier operations completed and preserve accepted updates and successful downloads. Retry only the failed review with bounded evidence, then validate returned source spans and field coverage. Successful retrieval alone does not establish recovery of the requested field.

decisions.reason: All six occurrences were inspected. Rows 4, 14, 19 and 20 each have one nonverbatim source association; row 24 has two. Every affected cell also has one matching source. The final code selects a matching source with next(), and earlier checks use any(), whereas the citation results evaluate each attached URL. Thus the concrete failure is per-source provenance, not demonstrated invention of all six quote strings. Existing generic quotation guidance did not prevent it; the memory update adds representation-aware validation without sacrificing semantic support.

All 52 occurrences concern verification after the initial ten discovery records identified 28 entities: nine group nationality searches, nine affiliation searches, two PDF searches, 26 individual nationality searches and six targeted follow-ups. All searches returned hits. Empty discovery arrays therefore do not establish stalled verification. The existing discovery memory explicitly requires honest empty records for known-entity verification, and the trajectory follows it. Its prior and current outcomes do not justify weakening or duplicating that guidance.

All 19 failures were reviewed: nine HTTP 403s, two HTTP 404s, three redirect loops, three unreadable-text failures, one timeout and one closed connection. Other sources and cached successes enabled progress; all final cited URLs have successful fetch records. The existing alternate-source skill already covers retaining successes and seeking actual alternative URLs. These observations do not establish successful repair of the failed endpoints or warrant endpoint-specific rules. The separate input-size candidate supports the targeted skill extension.

The call exceeded the 1,048,576-character input limit with 1,202,710 characters after five affiliation updates had already been accepted. Recovery retained those updates and used merged exact-source windows totaling 25,212 excerpt characters; the subsequent review completed without stderr. This successful repeatable recovery belongs in the existing evidence-extraction skill, with serialized-size checks before submission.

The assertion blocked a patch whose quote combined two source excerpts with added curly quotation marks. Diagnostics showed no unknown sources but no matching quotation. A single exact annual-report span repaired the patch, and later validation passed. Recovery is evidence for retaining the guard, not dismissing the failure; the provenance memory adds exact-span construction and targeted repair while addressing the remaining multi-source mismatch.

The execution reported zero nationality cells filled while submitting a recovery claim; the next diagnostic explicitly corrected that premise. Existing entry 2 already addresses this exact failure with measured before/after coverage and separate retrieval versus field recovery. Its version history includes the correction; the single recorded failed run does not show repeated failure of that revised instruction. No further edit is needed.

The auxiliary audit reported no unresolved support while deterministic membership testing found one PDF quotation mismatch. Inspection and exact-source replacement repaired it before finalization. This independently supports validating audit quotes rather than trusting semantic approval, and checking that the replacement still supports the stated claim. It shares the provenance update rather than creating a duplicate entry.

The reviewed records show useful reconciliation of dated roles, concurrent affiliations and later citizenship, plus full-source review of components omitted from selected quotations. They also show that reviewer objections need adjudication rather than automatic acceptance. Existing entry 2 already preserves this procedure and distinguishes semantic completeness from mechanical checks. Remaining quotation-provenance weaknesses are handled by the accepted update; no separate historical or benchmark-specific lesson is warranted.
